cues.text: Here are the options for that question.
Option A: reducing the total number of IT staff.
Option B: aligning IT strategy with business value.
Option C: regularly updating hardware and software systems.
Option D: creating various brand new programming languages.
The suggested answer is B.
Governance directs technology toward business value, while managing risk and accountability.
So the point of IT governance is not cutting staff, not simply keeping systems current, and certainly not inventing new languages.
It is about making sure technology serves what the business is trying to achieve.
Now to continuous assessment question twenty-five.
The purpose of a Service Level Agreement, or SLA, is to: Option A: limit support tickets.
Option B: guarantee total uptime.
Option C: set compensation rates.
Option D: define service expectations.
The suggested answer is D.
An SLA defines agreed service targets and responsibilities, not guaranteed perfect uptime.
That is why option B is tempting but wrong: an SLA sets out what level of service is expected and who is responsible, rather than promising that nothing will ever go down.
Next, continuous assessment question thirty-three.
Which IT governance framework is primarily strategic and focuses on enabling executive decision-making?
Option A: the ITIL framework.
Option B: the PCI-DSS standard.
Option C: the COBIT framework.
Option D: the ISO/IEC 38500 standard.
The suggested answer is D.
ISO/IEC 38500 is specifically directed at governing bodies and executive oversight.
COBIT is also strategic, but it has broader governance and management objectives.
So when the question asks which framework is primarily about enabling executive decision-making, ISO/IEC 38500 is the best fit, because of its direct focus on governing bodies.
